title: Increase the other electric charge
hook: Change second charge magnitude and predict electric-force magnitude.
misconception: electric-force magnitude stays fixed when second charge magnitude doubles.
objective: Apply F = k·abs(q₁q₂)/r² to compare electric-force magnitude when second charge magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With two fixed point charges at fixed separation in the same medium, F = k·abs(q₁q₂)/r². When second charge magnitude doubles, electric-force magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model F = k·abs(q₁q₂)/r²; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider two fixed point charges at fixed separation in the same medium, with a nonzero initial result. If second charge magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on electric-force magnitude?
recall.why: Apply F = k·abs(q₁q₂)/r² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
